To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polarization diversity can improve the performance of spatially multiplexed MIMO systems and can degrade the performance of MIMO systems employing transmit diversity.
the performance of polarization diversity in MIMO systems is strongly dependent on MIMO configuration (number of antennas and their spacing) and on the scattering environment.

the performance of spatially multiplexed MIMO signaling techniques can be improved significantly by employing polarization diversity, while the use of polarization-diverse antennas is detrimental for transmit diversity techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low-complexity, high-performance MIMO signaling techniques that can be employed in the presence of antenna diversity and polarization diversity.
the performance analysis of MIMO systems with dual-polarized antenna structures.
the design of cost-effective and space-effective MIMO antenna systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

polarization diversity is beneficial for spatial multiplexing in the sense of improving the average symbol error rate, while it is detrimental to the average symbol error performance of transmit diversity.
the use of polarization-diversity is beneficial for spatial multiplexing but not for transmit diversity.
the use of polarization-diversity in MIMO systems can be advantageous in some cases, but it is not a panacea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the case of polarization diversity, the performance of spatial-multiplexing techniques is improved, while the performance of transmit-diversity techniques is degraded.
polarization diversity does not provide any significant advantage for the Alamouti scheme.
the use of polarization in MIMO wireless communication systems is beneficial for spatial multiplexing but detrimental for transmit diversity techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of spatially multiplexed and transmit diversity MIMO systems is highly dependent on polarization diversity, and that in some cases, the use of polarization-diverse MIMO systems may yield significant performance benefits.
polarization diversity can be used to improve performance of spatial multiplicity, but not of diversity techniques.
polarization diversity may be a cost- and space- effective alternative to spatial diversity, especially in the context of spatial multiplexed MIMO systems.
